task1_email_traps.why_it_hurts: Missing even one required point lowers content score significantly.
task1_email_traps.fix: Turn every bullet point into one paragraph or clear section.

task1_email_traps.why_it_hurts: Using informal language in a complaint or formal request reduces coherence and task fulfillment.
task1_email_traps.fix: Use polite and professional language unless writing to a close friend.

task1_email_traps.why_it_hurts: Responses under 140 words usually lack development and detail.
Long responses increase grammar mistakes and waste time.

task1_email_traps.fix: Use introduction, body paragraphs, and a short closing.

task1_email_traps.why_it_hurts: Incorrect word usage hurts vocabulary and coherence scores.
task1_email_traps.fix: Use simpler words correctly rather than difficult words incorrectly.

task1_email_traps.why_it_hurts: The purpose of the email becomes unclear.
task1_email_traps.fix: Clearly state what action you want from the reader.

task1_email_traps.why_it_hurts: Frequent tense shifts lower grammar accuracy.
task1_email_traps.fix: Maintain consistent past, present, or future tense.

task2_survey_traps.why_it_hurts: Weak position lowers coherence and argument quality.
task2_survey_traps.fix: Choose one option strongly and support it.
Use specific examples and practical situations.
Use different arguments for each paragraph.
Include at least one realistic example.

task2_survey_traps.why_it_hurts: The essay becomes difficult to read.
task2_survey_traps.fix: Use one main idea per paragraph.

task2_survey_traps.why_it_hurts: Responses may sound unnatural or repetitive.
task2_survey_traps.fix: Use templates only as structure support.

task2_survey_traps.why_it_hurts: Trying to sound advanced can reduce clarity.
task2_survey_traps.fix: Use clear sentences with controlled complexity.
End with a direct summary of your opinion.

general_scoring_tips: Keep ideas clear and easy to follow.
Focus on clarity more than difficult vocabulary.
Manage time carefully: do not spend too long planning.
